purpose: Create a dynamic enemy-targeting system that considers player threat, physical presence, support actions, survival and enemy intelligence.
core_principles: Every player begins with 100 base aggro.
Aggro determines how much attention a player attracts from enemies.
Different enemy intelligence levels influence targeting behaviour.
Enemy personalities and instincts may influence target selection.
The system should remain easy for the DM to manage.
Do not introduce unnecessary bookkeeping or complexity.
Unresolved mechanics must remain unresolved until the DM decides.

rules: Every size category changes aggro by 5.
Medium size is neutral.
Average-INT and High-INT enemies ignore size-based aggro adjustments.

charisma_based_aggro.ability_used: Actual CHA ability score, not CHA modifier.
rules: Every CHA point above 10 reduces aggro by 2.
Every CHA point below 10 increases aggro by 2.
CHA 10 produces 100 baseline aggro.
Higher CHA reduces aggro.
Lower CHA increases aggro.
CHA reduction can stack with Stealth reduction.
unresolved: No minimum aggro multiplier or lower cap has been finalized.

stealth_based_aggro.ability_used: Stealth skill modifier, not DEX score.
conditions: The player must remain unseen by the enemy.
The player must not physically interact with or touch the enemy in a way that reveals their presence.
If the enemy notices the player, Stealth-based aggro reduction is cancelled.
Attacking, healing or providing support may reveal the player depending on the situation.

rules: CHA and Stealth reductions can stack.
Stealth is conditional and may be cancelled when the enemy notices the player.
Normal characters generate 1 aggro per 1 damage.
Tanks generate 2 aggro per 1 damage.
The tank multiplier compensates for typically lower damage output and helps tanks maintain enemy attention.
Healing generates aggro.
Only effective HP restored generates aggro.
Overhealing does not generate aggro.
Healing-generated aggro belongs to the healer, not the healed player.
A healer can become the highest-aggro target if their generated healing aggro surpasses other players' aggro.
unresolved: The exact healing-to-aggro conversion ratio has not been decided.

enemy_types: Other enemies capable of tactical reasoning
intelligent_enemy_support_detection.trigger: An intelligent enemy identifies a player operating in a rear-guard support role.
procedure: The identified player makes a CHA check.
On success, the player receives no additional aggro from this check.
On failure, the player gains a small amount of additional aggro.
dm_controlled: The DM determines the check DC.
The DM determines the additional aggro gained.
Both values depend on the situation and enemy.

rules: Losing HP generates additional aggro.
Intentionally taking damage to generate aggro is allowed under the current design.
The DM considers this acceptable because deliberately taking damage endangers the player.
Every player turn without attacking or healing reduces accumulated aggro by 5.
Attacking prevents aggro decay for that turn.
Healing prevents aggro decay for that turn.
Movement does not prevent decay.
Defensive actions do not prevent decay.
Utility actions do not prevent decay.
Defensive or utility actions only prevent decay if they also involve attacking or healing.
Aggro cannot fall below 0.
Decay applies to all accumulated aggro, not just base aggro.
aggro_decay.design_decision: Small attacks can reset decay. This is an intentional tactical trade-off because attacking can endanger teammates.

rules: Players at 0 HP retain their accumulated aggro.
Unconscious players cannot generate additional aggro.
unresolved: Whether retained aggro becomes active again immediately upon revival has not been explicitly finalized.

aggro_ties.resolution: The DM decides which player the enemy targets when multiple players have equal aggro.

enemy_targeting_instincts.description: Different enemy species and creatures may have different instincts, personalities and combat priorities that influence their target selection.
rules: These are behavioural tendencies, not mandatory rules.
Enemy instincts may influence targeting beyond numerical aggro.
Different species should not necessarily target the same way.
The DM should retain control over enemy behaviour.
design_restrictions: Do not create a separate aggro table for every enemy species.
The method of combining shared aggro values with different enemy instincts remains undecided.

Low_INT.behaviour: More influenced by physical presence and instinctive targeting.

Average_INT.behaviour: Uses the general aggro system without size-based adjustments.

High_INT.behaviour: Can identify rear-guard support and use tactical targeting behaviour.

notes: Numerical INT thresholds for these categories have not been established.
The DM may design intelligent enemies with special targeting behaviour.

rules: Taunts and special aggro manipulation may exist.
Their effectiveness depends on enemy intelligence, species and design.
The DM may control whether an enemy responds to a taunt.
There is no finalized universal taunt mechanic.

proximity_based_aggro.reason: Tracking aggro adjustments every time a player moves would waste DM time.

individual_enemy_aggro_tables.reason: Maintaining separate aggro tables for every enemy would be unnecessarily complicated.

unresolved_mechanics.detail: How much aggro is generated per effective HP restored?
Should aggro be calculated separately for each enemy based on damage received, or once using total damage dealt?
How should different enemy personalities influence target selection while retaining a shared aggro system?
The exact mathematical sequence for combining base aggro, passive adjustments and generated aggro has not been formally finalized.
Should retained aggro become active again immediately when a player is revived?
No universal minimum or maximum aggro cap has been finalized.
Numerical INT thresholds for Low-INT, Average-INT and High-INT enemies have not been established.

design_preferences.complexity: Keep the system manageable for a DM.
design_preferences.development_style: Develop mechanics step by step with the DM making final decisions.
avoid: Separate aggro tables for every enemy
design_preferences.priority: Gameplay balance, tactical decision-making and ease of use.

instructions_for_future_development: Treat all established mechanics as existing rules.
Do not silently change numerical values or formulas.
Do not treat unresolved mechanics as finalized.
Ask for the DM's approval before introducing or changing a mechanic.
When identifying loopholes, distinguish intentional tactical trade-offs from genuine exploits.
The DM has currently decided not to add more mechanics until further testing.
